To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SA and ABA, applied to the medium, can be used to alleviate the negative effects of osmotic stresses on wheat seedlings.

exogenous application of SA and ABA alleviates the negative effects of osmotic (PEG) stress in wheat seedlings by increasing the content of proline and carbohydrates as well as antioxidant activity, which results in a higher yield in the tolerant wheat variety compared to the susceptible one.

SA and ABA applied exogenously to wheat seedlings grown under hydroponic conditions in the presence of PEG, which induces osmotic stress, alleviate the negative effects of the stress, especially in the drought resistant cultivar.

the role of SA and ABA in the response to water deficit of wheat cultivars.
the effects of exogenously-applied SA and ABA on wheat seedlings under osmotic stress.
the alleviation of stress effects by exogenous application of salicylic and abscislic acids.
